elements.id-string-11: \abstract{In this paper we describe the differential geometric properties of a quantum scalar field in terms of Hida-Malliavin calculus.
elements.id-string-12: We focus our attention on the role played by the different mathematical structures of the Cauchy hypersurface which constitutes the domain of the classical fields and the geometrical structures that the classical field phase-space is endowed with.
elements.id-string-13: We argue that the classical phase space must be modelled over the strong dual of a Nuclear Frechèt space and it is endowed with a complex structure, which allows to define a Kähler structure on it using the canonical symplectic structure.
elements.id-string-14: This mathematical structure determines all required ingredients to describe quantum objects through a geometric quantization procedure, analogous to the usual construction on a classical mechanics phase space.
elements.id-string-15: We will discuss in detail two different polarizations, one complex and one real; and will compare three different quantizations frequently used in Physics: the usual Schrödinger quantization, the analogous one using the field-momenta instead of the fields; and holomorphic quantization based on creation and annihilation operators.
elements.id-string-16: We will see how the necessary ingredients of the quantization procedures take a simple form when written in terms of Malliavin tools.
elements.id-string-17: In the subsequent paper, these tools will be used to characterize the set of quantum states as a Poisson manifold and the unitary dynamics generated by Schrödinger formalism as integral curves of a Hamiltonian vector field.\textbf{Keywords: }Quantum fields,  Malliavin calculus, Schrödinger Picture, Holomorphic Picture, Momentum-field Picture, Infinite dimensional Fourier transform, Infinite dimensional Segal-Bargmann Transform, Infinite dimensional geometry}
elements.id-string-19: The mathematical description of Quantum Field Theory on an arbitrary background has always been a complicated task.

elements.id-string-21: That approach proved to be very successful in encoding the properties of quantum operators and states in a mathematically consistent framework.
elements.id-string-22: Nonetheless, it did not consider other mathematical aspects of the description, as  the differential geometric ones; which were not described in detail either in the other main mathematical approach to QFT, non-commutative geometry (\cite{connesNoncommutativeGeometry1994,connesRenormalizationQuantumField2000}), more focused, again, on algebraic tools.
elements.id-string-23: In particular, the geometrical description of the space of fields justifying, for instance, the existence of a Poisson bracket or of a symplectic form, relays on the definition of the suitable differentiable structure on the fields phase-space, which in this case is cumbersome to build.
elements.id-string-24: Furthermore, one of our interests in this construction comes from its potential use in a hybrid quantum-classical model which couples the quantum field and a classical gravitational field.

elements.id-string-406: Geometric quantization I: the general framework
elements.id-string-407: The goal of this section is to build the quantum field theory corresponding to the classical model presented above.
elements.id-string-408: As our goal is a geometric description of the resulting quantum model, we will consider a geometric quantization framework adapted to our infinite dimensional manifold.
elements.id-string-409: The procedure is, roughly speaking, similar to the usual construction on finite dimensional symplectic manifolds (see \cite{Woodhouse1997}), and based in two steps.
elements.id-string-410: a pre-quantization which builds an initial Hilbert space as the set of sections of a complex line bundle defined on the classical phase space and a representation of classical functions as operators on that set,and the definition of a polarization, which chooses a Lagrangian submanifold on the phase space of fields, defines the Hilbert space as the space of sections restricted to the submanifold and the operators as those preserving it in a suitable way.
elements.id-string-411: The first step is straightforward and relatively simple to define for a general symplectic classical manifold.
elements.id-string-412: The definition of the polarization is a more subtle task and introduces arbitrary choices which restrict the set of classical magnitudes that can be quantized.
elements.id-string-413: We will present now, first the general construction adapted to our manifold of fields.
elements.id-string-414: Then, we will exploit the Kähler structure we defined on $\mathcal{M}_C$ to consider one particular type of polarization, the holomorphic polarization, which exhibits several nice properties and largely simplifies the technicalities of the construction.
elements.id-string-415: Finally, we will compare the resulting construction with the usual approach based on a real polarization.
